title: Nice to meet you!

learn.title: be: affirmative and negative
learn.html:
be is used to talk about people, things and facts about them: name, age, origin, job. In Spanish this is split between ser and estar, but in English it always needs a subject.

SubjectAffirmativeNegative
II am (I'm) from León.I am not (I'm not) from León.
YouYou are (You're) from León.You are not (You aren't / You're not) from León.
He / She / ItHe is (He's) from León.He is not (He isn't / He's not) from León.
WeWe are (We're) from León.We are not (We aren't / We're not) from León.
TheyThey are (They're) from León.They are not (They aren't / They're not) from León.

With I, the negative is only "I'm not". "I amn't" is not used.

watch.right: He is from Mexico. / It is a big city.

learn.title: be: Yes/No questions and short answers
learn.html:
Used to ask if something is true or false. You make it by switching the order: be + subject.

AffirmativeNegativeQuestionShort answer
You are from Mexico.You aren't from Mexico.Are you from Mexico?Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
He/She/It is from Mexico.He/She/It isn't from Mexico.Is he/she/it from Mexico?Yes, he/she/it is. / No, he/she/it isn't.
We are from Mexico.We aren't from Mexico.Are we from Mexico?Yes, we are. / No, we're not.
They are from Mexico.They aren't from Mexico.Are they from Mexico?Yes, they are. / No, they aren't.
  • Answer with the pronoun (she, he, they), not with the name. For people, don't use it.
  • In a positive short answer, don't contract: Yes, I am. (not Yes, I'm.)

watch.why: Switch be and the subject. Intonation alone is not enough.
"it" is only for things and animals.
Positive short answers are not contracted.

learn.title: Age and personal facts: be, not have
learn.html:
In Spanish you have an age, but in English you are an age: I am 25 (years old).

AffirmativeNegativeQuestionShort answer
She is 25 (years old).She isn't 25.How old is she? / Is she 25?She's 25. / Yes, she is.

learn.title: Ordinal numbers and dates
learn.html:
They put things in order (first, second…) and, above all, they are used to say dates. Most end in -th: fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eleventh, thirteenth, twentieth. Three are irregular: first (1st), second (2nd), third (3rd), and they repeat in compound numbers: twenty-first (21st), twenty-second (22nd), twenty-third (23rd).

Spelling changes: five → fifth, eight → eighth, nine → ninth, twelve → twelfth, twenty → twentieth, thirty → thirtieth.

StructureExample
Month + ordinalMy birthday is on August 13th.
the + ordinal + of + monthMy birthday is on the thirteenth of August.
Day + the + ordinalMy next class is on Tuesday the eleventh.

watch.wrong: My birthday is the 13 of August.

learn.title: be: information questions (Wh-)
learn.html:
Use these when you want an answer about a thing, person, place, time, age, etc. The question word goes first, then be + subject.

WordQuestionAsks for…
WhatWhat is your name? / What is your address?thing, fact
WhereWhere are you from? / Where is Marta?place
WhenWhen is your birthday?date, time
WhoWho are you? / Who is Luis Tosar?person
How oldHow old are you?age

Common contractions: What's your name?, Where's Marta?, When's your birthday?, Who's your brother?

watch.why: Switch the order: be goes before the subject.

watch.wrong: How many years do you have?

learn.title: Useful expressions
learn.html:
• Nice to meet you. — when you meet someone; the answer is Nice to meet you, too.
  • Hi, I'm Paolo. / My name's Paolo. — to introduce yourself.
  • Where are you from? — I'm from Madrid. And you? — to ask and say where you are from.
  • Can you spell that, please? — when you don't understand how a name is spelled.
  • Can you repeat that, please? — when you didn't hear something.
  • Can you speak more slowly, please? — when people talk very fast.
  • What does that mean? — when you don't understand a word.
  • How do you say "…" in English? — when a word is missing.
  • Can you help me? — Yes, of course. — to ask for help.
  • Excuse me, … — to get attention before you ask something.
  • Thank you. / Thanks. — You're welcome. — to say thank you and reply.
  • Can I have your passport, please? — Yes, here you go. — at a hotel desk or at the airport.
  • Enjoy your stay. — what hotel staff say when they give you the key.
  • Yes, that's right. — to confirm a fact.

reading.title: Hi from Guadalajara!
paragraphs: Hi Kevin! Nice to meet you online. My name is Daniela Ruiz and I'm 22 years old. I'm from Guadalajara, Mexico, but I'm not there now. I'm a student at a university in Monterrey, and I have a part-time job in a store.
I study computer science. My best friend is Paola. She is in my class and she is from Puebla. Paola isn't 22. She is 21. Her birthday is on March 5th. My birthday is on October 13th.

My interests are music, movies and soccer. My brother isn't a student. He is 17, and his interests are video games and sports. I speak Spanish and a little English. Is English your first language? Where are you from? What is your phone number? Write to me soon!
